I just have to remember more of Jest’s life and see if he can defeat the Sword Divines." Kent had absolute trust in himself as Jest that he would be able to, despite not yet having memories of that.
He was about to face off against the Ten-Star Sword God when the memory key he used expired.
But being in Jest’s body and feeling what he felt, he knew the bastard wasn’t known as the greatest swordsman to ever live for nothing.
"I believe in myself, and I know I can do it."
"As for the others, thanks to Jest and my own efforts, I will get it done one of these days."
Kent then checked to see how many memory keys were left.
However, to his shock, all four keys were used up.
This left a small smile on his lips.
"It is to be expected.
I have been in there for a while, after all."
Kent looked at the many requirements he would have to personally handle and shook his head.
"This isn’t even the requirement to become a Sword Emperor."
Kent wanted to sigh again, but he knew sighing too much would make him look weak, so he decided to check the requirements for the Sword Emperor stage.
⟦Requirements to become a Sword Emperor⟧
↠ Defeat the Seven Horn Nightmare Devastating Shark Beast.
↠ Win the Mount Genesis Supreme Sword Competition.
Only two requirements, but Kent knew they would not be easy to handle.
First, despite not meeting this beast just yet, he already knew it wouldn’t be an easy battle.
Kent had a nagging feeling he had yet to meet a true challenge.
Of course, in a way, he was thrilled about it.
However, he knew he must prepare.
As for the second requirement, Kent was looking forward to it.
A sword competition doesn’t depend on one’s strength.
It only focuses on sword mastery, so if he wanted to win, then he must prepare well, because his overpowered Blood Cores would not help him.
It would be a pure battle between swordsmen to see who was the best.
"This means I must focus on awakening my sword realm.
Although I am Lord Genesis, there are monsters out there, so I cannot slack off."
It was going to be hard for sure, but Kent had already seen the path forward, so he planned to walk it to the end.
After all, there was no telling just what was waiting for him in this sword competition.
Since he had no more memory keys for Jest, he decided to make the next best thing: refine the two Blood Life Seals and the two Blood Death Seals in his possession.
This way, not only would he be hard to kill, but his killing intent would also become much more potent.
Aside from that, his sword intent would become much more potent as well.
Four seals appeared, and his two blood cores and flame core came to life.
He began refining them right away.
’I have three memory keys for the faceless assassin.
For now, I will hold on to them.
Once I have some free time on my journey to find Elina, I will review them.’
Kent smiled and sent his mind back to refining the four seals.
Months passed, but since it was tower time, he didn’t seem to care.
His ladies were out of harm’s way, and his legions were also recovering, so there was no telling just what he had to worry about.
On the outside, people searching for Kent had started dying in strange ways.
This caused most to run back to the Immortal World.
Uncle Drew went out to buy ingredients, but as a side quest, whenever he met someone who was searching for Kent, he didn’t hesitate to dispose of them.
Now, everyone was afraid to even look for him.
They didn’t want to die unexpectedly and tragically.
Soon, five years passed inside the tower.
On this day, the four seals were done being refined, so Kent decided to absorb them.
For precautionary purposes, he first chose to absorb the Blood Life Seals before focusing on the Blood Death Seals.
Something that enhances his killing intent was not something to be taken lightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 1160: First Blood Cleansing Bath
paragraphs: "Damn."
Kent muttered, watching the red mist swirl around him.
He had finished absorbing the blood death seals, and the result is intent manifestation.
Intent manifestation is something only seasoned killers can do.
They said that when one had their fair share of slaughter, their intent could no longer remain within them, so it would erupt into whatever shapes they deem fit for it.
Whenever they use it, those with enough experience can shape it into any form they desire. However, it takes thousands, perhaps even millions of years of slaughter to achieve that.
Kent had reached the initial stage of intent manifestation to the shock of anyone who would be at the receiving end of his killing intent.
Although he could not manifest and shape it into any form he wanted, he could at least let it become visible.
That is more than enough for someone in a High World.
"I just have to be careful I don’t accidentally scare my enemies to death," he smiled, stood up, and stretched. The Blood Life Seals had turned him into an immortal.
Regenerating body parts is now possible. He could not regenerate them within seconds, but he could within minutes.
That is better than none, and knowing he would soon be getting more seals, he could only allow himself to feel happy before turning to his next task.
Kent walked toward a glass bath filled with blood. Even from 30 meters away, he could sense the feeling of bloodlust emanating from it.
"So I have to bathe in this thing." Kent took a deep breath, taking steady steps toward the bath.
⟦The master must have his Blood Cleansing bath every now and then to strengthen his bloodlust. It is ideal to have a powerful bloodlust when one is walking the sword path.⟧
Kent couldn’t deny that. He had already received the complete blood path manual from the Slaughter King, so he knew what had to be done.
However, feeling the danger coming off the bloodbath, he couldn’t help wondering just what would become of him after bathing in this blood.

His mind went back to when Chaos had his first bloodbath. Back then, he entered a bloodthirsty state where, for 12 months, he killed senselessly, causing great panic to spread far and wide in the Blood System.
Many immortals fled their homes just to escape the wrath of the Chaos Dragon. Many, of course, weren’t that lucky.

The bloodlust is meant to make him strong, but it has a side effect. Mostly, this side effect makes in ultra stronger, but at the expense of hurting even his allies when he is lost in the blood realm.
⟦The master shouldn’t worry. I have already created contingency plans to keep you contained should you enter a bloodthirsty state after the Blood Cleansing bath.⟧
"Thank you, Tower."
Kent soon reached the bath and stripped naked before raising his body, submerging himself in the blood. Gaia appeared inside the tower and added three treasures to the blood.
Soon, the bath closed, and the blood began to boil.
"Happy bath, master," she smiled and left the Sword Tower to go play with Kent’s mom, who had come out of seclusion.
Years had passed already since she entered the Cultivation Garden.

Meanwhile, inside the Legion Tower, Vexthra was having a meeting with the legion and her sisters. Alina had woken up thanks to the pill Yuna made for her. However, she was still too weak to do anything.
However, she was in attendance.
"I have received word from the Foxkins on Planet Fedora that the Orc King is out, and he is planning on making a move to completely crush them and their allies.
The Fox king had become a Spirit Lord, but surprisingly, the Tyrant King Balma had reached the Heavenly Ascension Stage, and he even has five more Spirit Lords under his command.
Also, some people are helping them from the shadows. This is why they want us to come help them before it is too late." Vexthra paused and observed everyone’s expression.
"I know some of you haven’t fully recovered yet, so you are out, but those of you who can fight, we will be leaving soon, so prepare."
Alina sighed, knowing that even if she wanted to, she just couldn’t afford to create any array or formation in her current condition.
Aside from her, some of her sisters and even the Eternal Wrath Legion also can’t join. Vexthra will not allow them since they are still recovering.
"Maybe I alone should go and crash their hopes and dreams," Uncle Drew, who was seated on the side, eating Spirit Grapes, said.
Vexthra glared at him and smirked, "When we meet an Immortal, you will step in; until then, I will advise you to run back to the underworld. We don’t need you."
"True, we don’t need a cheat," Kaizo, who knew that with Uncle Drew around, his status as the strongest was threatened, said, supporting the goddess.
Uncle Drew smiled weakly and snapped his finger. A green flaming portal opened, and from within, a pair of identical twins walked out, one holding a bow, the other a scythe.
"How about allowing Ivy and Olive to help in my stead? They are Empyreans. If you want, I can even suppress their cultivation to the Heavenly Ascension Stage to make things fair."
Vexthra and everyone could only look at the Night Rider Captain as if he were some kind of monster.
In the universe, the Forsaken Race are beings who are not affected by the restrictions on worlds. They can maintain their cultivation in any world they find themselves in.
Aside from them, the Chaos and Void Beasts are the same. They have no restrictions on them.
There are others out there...

However, aside from them, there were the Night Riders, said to be the greatest warriors to grace the universe. Their captain, Kael Duskbane, was the right-hand man of the Wraith Queen who ruled Ebonviel and the greatest warrior to ever live.
Not even the Chaos Dragon or the Blood Spear King came close to his prowess on the battlefield.
Now, this same person, whom many demons ran from, casually sat pulling warriors that could bring down worlds within minutes out of nowhere.
Uncle Drew didn’t go down to the underworld to play. He had created several Night Agents. The weakest of them is Olive, and her twin sister Ivy is next.
Vexthra looked at Uncle Drew for a few minutes and sighed, "Fine, they can join, but they are prohibited from killing the Spirit Kings and below. Also, they cannot touch the Orc King.
Lastly, they cannot quickly kill the beings hidden in the shadows. It must be slow and painful."
Ivy and Olive smiled, looking at their master, who gave them a wink.
Then they bowed slightly to Vexthra. "Rest assured, goddess, we will make sure death is a luxury to them."
Kaizo and everyone shuddered as they looked at the twins’ smiles.
Uncle Drew looked at Nara, Saden, and Eryndor, his teammates, and asked, "You still don’t want me to break the seal, huh?"
Uncle Drew wants to break their Night Seals so they can level up much quickly and also not get affected by the restrictions in High worlds.
Nara shook her head, "We want to first reach our limits before doing that."
"I see. In any case, you three should kill at least 5,000 each. If you lag behind, you will be spending 2,000 years in hell as punishment."
The three shuddered and promptly nodded, "We will not disappoint you, Captain."
Uncle Drew nodded, "I hope so."
Vexthra looked at Nara, who seemed shaken by the idea of her spending 2,000 years in hell. Seeing her sister scared, she glared at Uncle Drew.
"I know you want them strong and all, but you should know Nara is your master’s wife. I hope you get what I am trying to say."
Uncle Drew smiled, "Loud and clear, my goddess. But fear not, master will understand."
Vexthra smiled and copied Uncle Drew’s words, "I hope so."
What she meant to say was, ’Even if he understood, as long as I have boobs and a butt, he will listen to whatever I say.’
The Night Rider Captain shuddered at the sight of Vexthra’s smile.
"Alright, let’s get ready to leave."

chapters.title: Chapter 1161: True Blood Path
paragraphs: Six days passed in the blink of an eye, but Kent hadn’t emerged from the blood bath. His entire body had been submerged in the blood.
Initially, the blood was merely boiling. However, as days passed, it started to change color from deep red to green.
Obviously, that was a clear sign that Kent was either absorbing the essence from the blood or that something was coming out of his body, turning the blood green.
Either way, the aura around him seemed to grow by the minute, so he remained submerged.

On the seventh day, Kent suddenly burst out of the blood and hovered in the air. Soon, his body was cocooned. In that instant, Kent’s consciousness left his body and appeared in a place filled with so many flowers.
Sitting at the center of this flower field was a man Kent would never forget, even if he were blind.
Of course, seeing the Slaughter King in such a place came as a shock to him, but he swallowed his shock and walked toward him.
When he approached him, Kent sat down in a lotus posture and observed the man for a few seconds before a chuckle escaped his lips.
This chuckle seemed to have woken BhaalZhar up.

"I was 230 years, a recently ascended warrior only at the Empyrean stage, when my home world was suddenly invaded by 23,000 bandits, 400 of which were Life stage warriors and 100 Death stage warriors.
Those were beings two realms higher than me.
The strongest in my world then was a level 3 Death Stage Roc Beast. Naturally, that meant we were doomed.
The men would be killed, ladies taken to be sold into prostitution, and children groomed to serve other purposes once they were old enough.
It was a losing battle, and everyone knew that. There was no saving us from such odds.
However, for me, instead of seeing despair, I saw an opportunity to grow; I saw an opportunity to bathe in blood. I saw an opportunity to Slaughter.
And so it happened.
It took three hours, but by the time I was done, every last bandit had died. My pale white skin was drenched in red blood.
I became unrecognisable.
I earned the title The Slaughter King, and since then, not even gods dare mess with my world.
I went on and reached the peak of the Celestial stage, forming seven Blood Cores, 4,001 Blood Life seals, and 6,006 Blood Death seals.
Among the six primordials, I was the third strongest, and in terms of killing, none of them came close.
The reason why that was possible, of course, was thanks to the path I walked."
BhaalZhar opened his red eyes, causing Kent’s soul to shudder. Immediately, he felt weak, almost as if he was staring into the eye of death.
"I walked the Slaughter path. I walked the path of blood."
BhaalZhar blinked, and like it never happened, Kent could breathe again. He took a deep breath to calm his racing heart.
"You have become much stronger since the last time we met," BhaalZhar said, giving Kent an appraising look.
"How many cores have you formed?"
"Two... but yet to saturate them."

BhaalZhar nodded. "Now that you have finished your first blood cleansing bath, it will be a while before you will be able to saturate them. If my calculations are correct, just these two cores will take you to the peak of the Death stage.
Be sure to fully saturate them and absorb at least ten Blood Life and Death seals before forming the third Blood Core."
Kent nodded.
He had no plans to form his third Blood Core until he had fully awakened all Blood Seals. Naturally, that would take him far into the peak of the Death stage, like BhaalZhar said.
His path was now all about Slaughter, and Kent most certainly would love to go on a slaughter soon to reach the Spirit Lord stage.
"How about the Bone Tempering Art?"
"I have fully cultivated the first form, awakening 55,600 Blood Seals out of 105,600."
BhaalZhar raised his brow, clearly taken aback by what he had just heard. He in no way expected Kent to awaken so many Blood Seals.
Back when he was walking the blood path, he could only awaken 90,000 Blood Seals, making him the third-strongest and one of the most dangerous killers to ever walk the face of the Universe.
"I guess being the best of us is only right. Your journey is more important than ours," BhaalZhar smiled and then waved his hand, manifesting a manual.
"You won’t understand anything in it now, but memorize this," he said, handing it to Kent, who took it and began memorizing the manual.
After an hour, he was done, and the manual vanished into thin air
"Wonderful. Now, just wait and awaken all Blood Seals before you start forming the Blood Tattoos. The content you have memorized will activate when all Blood Seals have awakened.
Only then can you form the Blood Tattoos by cultivating the second form of the Bone Tempering Art."
Kent nodded again and decided to ask his own question.
"Do you think I am strong enough to learn the Claw Art?"
"No."
Kent smiles. He thought he was strong enough to learn the most terrifying technique in his arsenal, but it seemed he may have underestimated the technique.
"Not even the first form?"
BhaalZhar burst out in resounding laughter. "Brat, I created the first form of the technique when I was a Demigod and killed gods with it. The second and third forms were created when I became a god.
The Supremes stood no chance.
As for the fourth to the seventh forms, they were created when I became a Celestial. The Claw Art is one of the most dangerous techniques ever created.
Trust me, learning just the first form will turn you into a terror."
"Compared to the Finger of Destruction, which one is to be feared?"
"Oh, please, if you want to make a comparison, at least pick something decent," BhaalZhar sneered, feeling disdain at the mention of the Finger of Destruction.
"Among the Primordial techniques we created, the Finger of Destruction was the weakest of them. Even the Flame Beast King knew that, and that was why he gave it to the universe."
Kent shook his head and smiled.
He had learned the first form of the Finger of Destruction, yet he couldn’t even unleash five percent of its true power.
Even now that he was just two steps away from becoming a Spirit Lord, unleashing more than five percent of the technique was beyond him.
However, now hearing that what he saw to be the peak of techniques was merely a failed experiment thrown into the universe for mortals to fight over, he couldn’t help feeling like a failure.
"Just how strong were the Six True Primordials?"
BhaalZhar smiled and raised his shoulders. "We were the peak of existence. After us, none had ever come close to reaching the level we reached...not even you, the Chaos dragon.
We were the six great existences... Blood, Fire, Lightning, Darkness, Ice, and Metal.
Among the six of us, Metal was the strongest, followed by Lightning and then me. The fourth strongest was Fire, and the fifth went to Ice.
Darkness was the weakest yet the most difficult to kill.
Back then, when the time came, he was the last to fall.
When it came to survival, he was the best of us, and that was why he was also the one we chose to guard your life core.
In essence, Darkness was your father."

As for the fourth to the seventh forms, they were created when I became a Celestial.
The Claw Art is one of the most dangerous techniques ever created.
Trust me, learning just the first form will turn you into a terror."
"Compared to the Finger of Destruction, which one is to be feared?"
"Oh, please, if you want to make a comparison, at least pick something decent," BhaalZhar sneered, feeling disdain at the mention of the Finger of Destruction.
"Among the Primordial techniques we created, the Finger of Destruction was the weakest of them.
Even the Flame Beast King knew that, and that was why he gave it to the universe."
Kent shook his head and smiled.
He had learned the first form of the Finger of Destruction, yet he couldn’t even unleash five percent of its true power.
Even now that he was just two steps away from becoming a Spirit Lord, unleashing more than five percent of the technique was beyond him.
However, now hearing that what he saw to be the peak of techniques was merely a failed experiment thrown into the universe for mortals to fight over, he couldn’t help feeling like a failure.
"Just how strong were the Six True Primordials?"
BhaalZhar smiled and raised his shoulders.
"We were the peak of existence.
After us, none had ever come close to reaching the level we reached...not even you, the Chaos dragon.
We were the six great existences...
Blood, Fire, Lightning, Darkness, Ice, and Metal.
Among the six of us, Metal was the strongest, followed by Lightning and then me.
The fourth strongest was Fire, and the fifth went to Ice.
Darkness was the weakest yet the most difficult to kill.
Back then, when the time came, he was the last to fall.
When it came to survival, he was the best of us, and that was why he was also the one we chose to guard your life core.
In essence, Darkness was your father."

chapters.title: Chapter 1162: Darkness
paragraphs: Obviously, the last thing Kent expected to hear was who his original father was.
Kent is already aware that he was born from the same energy that made the Universe. He is aware that he is a True Primordial just like the six who had lived before him.

He is even aware that, aside from his life as the Chaos Dragon, he has lived other lives, of which one was Lord Genesis, the greatest swordsman to have ever lived, and the other was the Faceless Assassin, the most dangerous assassin known to the universe.
He had yet to learn more about his other lives, but he was confident they were exceptional people as well.
He knew this much because he had already started recalling the memories of the lives he had lived.
However, he never for one second questioned where his lineage came from.
He most certainly didn’t question how he came into being as the Chaos Dragon. Of course, Leviathan told him he was born from an egg, but he didn’t believe him.
But now, Bhaalzhar had hinted at what could be the biggest reveal in his life.
"This is too confusing," Kent said, feeling a slight headache
"Just who are the True Primordials? What was your purpose, and how do I fit into all of this?"
Bhaalzhar smiled and snapped his fingers, manifesting seven balls.
"I have already told you that the true overlords of the universes were the True Primordials... well, we still are the overlords, considering our influence still lives."
"What is that supposed to mean to me? Aren’t you guys already dead?"

"Technically, we are not dead. However, in terms of mundane understanding, we are indeed dead. And before you ask, know that I will not reveal anything, not when that will be putting your life in danger."
Kent didn’t say anything.
Bhaalzhar took a deep breath and added, "Though you must know that whatever we started, you will be the one to finish it."
Some things, like they say, are better left unsaid. However, Kent knew he had to learn about his lineage or at least know something.
Thankfully, he seems to have grasped something.
This time, Kent seemed to have thought of something, and so he shifted slightly and asked in a somewhat skeptical tone.
"Is the Celestial stage the strongest in the Universe?"
Speaking in coded language can sometimes come in handy when discussing moments that directly go against Karma and fate.
Kent knew some things were better said in code, so he asked a question that, when answered, would allow him to piece things together.
"I created the Claw Art when I reached the Demigod stage. It helped me kill gods, but my ambition goes beyond that.

I want to kill far stronger than that, so for the better part of my Godhood and Celestialhood, I focused on the technique, adding more forms to it. It has seven forms, and killing a Celestial needs at most the fourth form. Anything beyond that, and one would call you a madman."
Kent nodded, getting his answer.
However, now that he knew Celestials aren’t the peak, the question remains: why are there no beings stronger than Celestials in the universe now?
Sure, the Celestials are powerhouses.
They are beings who control the laws. They can shape reality to their liking, reverse time to prevent casualties, and even alter how the universe is perceived. They are terrifying beings.
So the idea that there are beings far stronger than that is just absurd. Kent knew for a fact that the Celestial stage is the peak of this universe.
So if that is the case, then where are they if there are people like that? How long have they been around? Where were they when the Universe nearly came to an end during the Primordial Era?
Kent knew Bhaalzhar was not going to answer him, but asking himself these questions made him get them out of his mind.
He also knows one day he will find answers to his question. Bhaalzhar merely dumped a big plot on him and decided not to answer any questions.
"Tell me about my father then."
In the end, asking about someone else makes sense. He knew Bhaalzhar exaggerated when he said his father was darkness.
"I cannot speak his name, for he will be the one to say it. Even our True Primordial names carry weight."
Kent nodded.

He is already aware of this. Even his own name holds some power that his followers can use to command others with his permission. Lyna used it when she came and handed the scroll to Runa, the High Priestess.
"However, I can tell you that Darkness was the most elusive of us all. Among the six of us, he is the hardest to kill.

It wasn’t because he had the most overpowered healing ability. He had none; however, he had the darkness, the shadows. He walked between the shadow and darkness, making him someone who could slip away anytime he wanted.
We have lived for a very long time, but not once has an enemy ever caught us him a trap. Back then, we called him a coward; however, we later found out that he is the opposite.
Killing him is hard. However, you also wouldn’t see him coming. Every shadow can be him; every darkness can manifest into a dangerous assassin.
So when the time came for you to be born, we handed your life crystal to him, for in his hands, we were assured he would accomplish the mission."
Bhaalzhar smiled. "And now that you are here, it seems we were right to give him your life crystal."
"Then he was more like a guardian, seeing that he only guarded my life crystal." Kent smiles, knowing his thinking is probably shallow.
Considering he wasn’t born the normal way, there is no telling who and what can be called his father or mother. So perhaps he had to accept whatever he got.

"Guardian, you say, that is true. However, to make sure you are born, one of us was to activate the creation process by ejecting our core essence into your life crystal. Darkness was the one who did that."
"I see. I guess I will be glad to meet him one of these days, then," he smiled, feeling somewhat happy.
"Oh, you will. After all, you already have one of his techniques," Bhaalzhar said, causing Kent to raise his brow. A second later, however, he understood what he meant.
"The Faceless Art."
Bhaalzhar smiled. "Indeed. The Faceless Art was one of his finest creations."
Kent couldn’t help but be impressed that his old man had created a technique that once made him the most dangerous assassin. Although he didn’t know him, he felt proud to learn this important detail.
"In fact, among the eighteen Primordial Techniques ever created, the Faceless Art is among the top five. What you have now is merely the first form.
There are still two more forms out there, and let me tell you, learning all three forms of the Faceless Art is going to make you a very dangerous person."
Bhaalzhar gave Kent a dubious smile and added, "Your mission is more important than us, so you must take everything there is to have."
Kent sighed and asked, "And what are those things?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1163: Path Forward
paragraphs: From the moment Kent met Bhaalzhar, he knew there was a much bigger role he would play in his life. He was, after all, a True Primordial just like himself.
So he was only waiting to learn more about what role the six Primordials would play in his life.
Now, Bhaalzhar seemed to have hinted at it, and so Kent wanted to know more.
Bhaalzhar smiled and looked into the distance before answering. "You really should take retrieving your memories more seriously. You have lived many lives after all, and so prioritize that.
Everything you are and will be depends on you recalling your thirteen lives."
And just like that, Bhaalzhar dodged the question. However, Kent wasn’t mad; he knew there was a much deeper meaning to all this.
Of course, the stronger he became, the more he could uncover without any severe backlashes. After everything is said and done, one of these days, he will get all the answers.
"You have to go back," Bhaalzhar said, and then added.

"Remember, though, before you form your third core, be sure to accomplish the following. Pay close attention because the chances of us meeting for a while are slim. There are five other True Primordials waiting for you out there..."
Kent nodded.
"First, you must know this. The reason the Chaos Dragon at his peak wasn’t even ten percent of the strength of the Six True Primordials was that it wasn’t yet your time.
He was meant to be the strongest of us, the True Primordials.
However, for that to happen, he must inherit our power, which you have started now. This also means no matter what, you must never miss even a single thing from us.
We have created our six paths, and once you get all, the True Primordial Chaos Dragon will be born."
Bhaalzhar smiled. "Your enemies are very strong, but you are the Chaos Dragon."
Kent felt his pride bubble up.

Being praised by an existence that transcends the limits of this universe was nice to some extent. However, he also knew his life would be hard, so paying attention was the best thing he could do now.
"Your path is the Blood Path. However, that is merely a way for you to level up. There are five other paths you need to inherit to awaken your true self."
Kent nodded again.
"Now, to what you must do. First, do not form the third core until both cores are saturated. This is a must, and you must do well to remember that.
Second, be sure to awaken all blood seals before forming the third core. Also, do not cultivate the second form of the Bone Tempering Art until all blood seals have been awakened.
Third, be sure to refine at least ten Blood Life and Death Seals. This is important, and you must ensure it is completed before the third core is formed.

Lastly, when you have refined at least ten Blood Life Seals, you can attempt learning the first form of the Claw Art. For now, don’t dare try, for it will be painful, and if care is not taken, your soul might even be affected.
So for now, stay away from it."
Kent nodded.

Bhaalzhar waved his hand, and a portal opened. "Remember this, learning too much has backlashes, so before you question the others, know that there is a reason we have Low, Medium, High, and Immortal worlds."
With that, Bhaalzhar waved his hand, and Kent was sent flying through the portal.
On the outside, the cocoon cracked, and from within, Kent emerged, a red mist spinning around him like a flexible halo.
When he opened his eyes, a powerful, red, misty flame aura burst out, sending a powerful killing intent spreading all around.
The feeling of dread filled the Sword Tower.
Kent, who could feel his strength and how dangerous he had become, smiled and then focused on stabilizing his aura.

It took him two good days to stabilize his aura to the stage where he wouldn’t scare those close to him. After that was settled, he got dressed and walked toward the Sword of Enlightenment again and sat down.
He first examined his aura by channeling it through his finger, watching the red mist swirl around it.
"Not exactly strong enough to rival an Immortal, but strong enough to shake their resolve." His first Blood Cleansing bath was a success.
Now, he could focus on other things and, hopefully, saturate his core quickly enough.

"My sword intent is now more dangerous than ever. If I can push both the intent and aura to the 9th level, I will be able to win the sword competition, which I have no idea when or where it will take place."

Kent wasn’t in a hurry, at least. He knew one way or another, he would find his way to this sword competition. Of course, before that, like Bhaalzhar said, he must handle a series of important things.
His core saturation, Blood Seals, Life and Death Seals, and even attempting to learn the Claw Art.
"At least I now know who my father was, so that is a bonus."
He smiled, sending his mind back to when Faceless received the Faceless Art from his mother. "To think the Faceless Art that got my mother killed was actually created by someone this close to me."
Kent shook his head.

The memories he had so far of his life as the Faceless Assassin only covered when he received the technique from his dying mother, and finally killing every last member of the Silent Shadow Assassin Organization.
The memory ended when he took on a mission to kill a certain tyrant king, who, no matter how many assassins they sent after him, none returned.
Kent didn’t know what would happen next, but he knew for sure it was going to be a good experience. For now, he was holding on to the memory keys.
However, now that he learned his old man created the Faceless Art, he might just review the memories much faster than he had planned to wait.
Of course, he wouldn’t be doing that just yet.
He still had something else to handle before he left seclusion to attend to other matters.
"Although I cannot create Primordial-grade techniques, I sure can create something that will devastate even Immortals."
Kent muttered, then calmly reached into his space ring and pulled out an item.
"Time to create my first flame technique."

chapters.title: Chapter 1164: Divine Flame Armament
paragraphs: Kent stood atop a mountain, gazing at the clear sky with a calm expression.
Hundreds of mountains stretched from the ground, rising into the air.
The mountain he stood on could be considered the shortest one.
All the other mountains were colossal, stretching many kilometers high.
However, he stood calmly, gazing at the clear sky as if he were waiting for something.
Naturally, he indeed was waiting for something.
Thankfully, what he was waiting for showed its face a couple of seconds later.
Suddenly, the sky started turning green, the thick clouds forming in what looked like a deadly storm. The air also seems to start heating up.
However, there was no storm; in fact, this was something completely opposite to a storm.
As the cloud formed, something metallic and colossal slowly emerged from it, instantly causing the ground to shake.
At first glance, one could see the knuckles of a right fist. As it slowly appeared, one could see a green and black metallic gauntlet, tightly clenched into a fist.
The pressure it exerted began shaking the very ground vigorously.
Even with only the knuckles up to the wrist showing, most of the mountains started crumbling. The heat and pressure bearing down on them were just too much to remain standing.
"Damn, now this is something I can work with," Kent muttered, wiping the sweat that had formed on his forehead.
Soon, the entire gauntlet had appeared, and its length alone was about 400 meters. The fist was also huge.
The pressure and heat were so severe that Kent felt suffocated just by standing beneath them.
The shocking part was that he stood 3 km away, but the pressure had spread to where he was, and as the gauntlet descended further, the pressure and the heat only seemed to intensify.
Kent raised his hand and gestured down.
As if being pushed by an external force, which it was, the gauntlet moved at great speed, and before Kent could blink, hundreds of mountains were wiped out.
GASP
Kent gasped as he opened his eyes on the outside. Sweat formed on his forehead, clearly from the pressure he was under while inside the skill space.
He had just witnessed the first form of his flame technique, which he created by sacrificing a bunch of flame techniques, including even divine-grade techniques.

In fact, aside from the Flame Wheels technique, all the techniques he had learned from the Flame Tower were gone, and the worst part was, they had been wiped from his mind, so he could not use them ever again.
However, he had created something powerful from it. The flame technique he had created was a weapon of mass destruction.
The gauntlet was the first form of the technique, yet it had already proven itself to be a dangerous one.
"Please tell me what I have just seen is the full capacity the first form can harness?" Kent smiled weakly, feeling his pride and emotions swelling up.
⟦The master had yet to fully realize the technique’s potential because he still lacked flame essence. At the moment, you can only use 50% of its true capacity 15 times before running out of energy.
Until the master can fully harness the true power of the first form, he cannot use the second form.⟧
"Damn, that is something to be happy about... right?"

⟦It is, master. The Divine Flame Armament technique is a good technique for you. Although it is nowhere close to the ranks of a Primordial technique, it will be more than enough for you to harness your flame in ways a true flame cultivator should.⟧
Kent smiled.

When he started creating the technique, he wanted something that could match the Finger of Destruction. However, he was shocked to learn he needed to sacrifice Supreme-grade and even Celestial-grade flame techniques to achieve that.
Naturally, he had no such technique to sacrifice, so he only focused on the divine-grade and below. Now he had created a technique that harnesses the power of his flame element to form weapons.
The first form is a gauntlet that can crush mountains into powder. Who is to say what the second form will be like?
"I need to form my second flame core now that I have formed the second blood core gate. That is the only way I can harness the true form of this technique."
⟦The master already has enough Primordial Flames to form the second core. However, I advise the master to find other flame-rich treasures to add to it.
Also, once the master forms the second flame core, the first one will expand further, making room to saturate it with more flame essence.
I yet again advise the master should find a flame-rich zone to undergo the procedure there.⟧
"In other words, I cannot form the second flame core just yet."
⟦Exactly.⟧
Kent took a deep sigh and then chose to push the matter about the flame core aside. He had formed his first flame technique.
It is only a god-grade technique, but since he can later upgrade it, there is no telling what it will become.

"With the Divine Flame Armament, not only would I be able to pay a visit to the Flame Demon Tower, but I can even find out where the other forms of the ’Finger of Destruction’ are and hopefully get my hands on them.
Although it is a failed experiment, it is still a primordial-grade flame technique."
After making up his mind, Kent switched to the mission he gave to the tower.

"Were you able to find a path that will lead to the edge of this galaxy much faster?" Before entering seclusion, he had tasked the tower with mapping the worlds he had been to and the ones like the sword worlds he had ways to reach and see whether she could create a path for him to follow.
⟦I have indeed found a path and even made a shocking discovery.⟧
"Oh... do tell."
⟦You can start your journey from Fedora, then move to Menelaus, and then to the Pyris Pill World. Then from there, you can move to Byrmrr...⟧
"Hold on... Byrmrr, I know this name."
Kent thought for a moment, then his face lit up with shock. He seemed to have recognized the name. "Byrmrr is the world Jest grew up in."
⟦That is true.⟧
"Wait a minute. How does that apply here? I have never been to that world, so naturally, that place shouldn’t register on the Planet Teleporter."
⟦That is indeed true. However, it seems now that you have ascended to a high world, the teleporter has started registering all those worlds.

"Wow, this is awesome."

"Let’s think about that later. For now, I just want to know what the ladies are up to."

chapters.title: Chapter 1165: Long Overdue Battle (1)
paragraphs: [Planet Fedora - Battleground]
The war that had been brewing for many years had finally reached its breaking point.
Years back, Fedora was a peaceful beast world where the various races of beasts lived in harmony.
Life was good.
In fact, there was nothing like war in the world.
Every race had its king or queen who saw to it that all their affairs were in order. They worked around the clock to provide for their people.
However, that peaceful and harmonious life came crashing down when the Orc King decided to become the Supreme Ruler of the entire planet.
The peace that guided their race for all these years came crashing down within weeks. Most of the races lost the fight, and so they were swallowed by the Orcs.
However, the Foxkin stood up and said no.
They weren’t as weak as the Orc King thought, and so, for a while, they held out while trying their best to pull the other races into an alliance.
Thankfully, just when everything was at the point of no return, Dori appeared and helped them pull through.
Years later, after Kent reunited with Dori, he also came through for them on multiple occasions. However, they knew one day they would have to fight for their freedom.
They had been preparing for that day for a while now.
Today, the battle they had been waiting for had finally arrived.
The Orc King brought with him the Orc army, Hellhounds, Lionkin, Batkin, and Rabbitkin. They numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
Naturally, for a small world like Fedora, that was a lot of warriors.
The Rebel Alliance, which comprised the Foxkin, Tigerkin, and Catkin, also stood on one side. They were led by King Hkum, who had reached Level 5 Spirit King.

The leader of the Catkin was a Level 3 Spirit King, and the leader of the Tigerkin was a Level 2 Spirit King. Aside from them, only Queen Amorian, who was the wife of the Fox King, and three others had also reached the Spirit King stage.
The rest are Spirit Sovereigns and below.
Meanwhile, the enemy had several Heavenly Ascension stage warriors, with even the Tyrant King miraculously reaching Level 8 Heavenly Ascension stage.
When Kent poisoned him, he was sure he would be comatose for a while. Now, it turned out that whoever was backing him was much more resourceful than he had expected.
The number of Spirit Kings in his army numbered over a hundred. That was more than the Rebel Alliance could handle.
It was also the main reason why King Hkum called for help from Kent’s legion. Kent is their guardian, so when danger came, they called for his help.
King Balma flew into the air and stopped when he was 200 meters away from the Rebel army. King Hkum also flew forward and made sure there were 50 meters between them.
That is a safe distance to ensure he wasn’t caught off guard.
"So you have finally shown your true colours, huh, Balma?" King Hkum said with a disdainful expression. They were friends before King Balma decided to become a Tyrant.

"No need to wear that expression. Just look around you, Hkum, this is all the more reason to surrender. You’ve already lost, and you know that," King Balma smiled and cast a glance at the pitiful number of warriors behind King Hkum.
"I wouldn’t be too sure about that, Balma. Unlike you, who relied on pills to reach where you are, we actually followed a good method, ensuring our foundation is solid.
So, despite you having the largest number of warriors, when it comes to true strength, you will see in a bit." King Hkum raised his voice so his enemy could hear him clearly...
"I just hope all of you are prepared to die."
King Balma smirked, and his army burst out in a round of laughter. This was their response to the warning King Hkum gave them.
They are prepared to slaughter their enemies without any remorse.
"In that case, there will be no surrender. So either your side is completely wiped out, or my side is. In any case, after today, the peace we once had will be restored."
After saying that, King Hkum turned and left, causing King Balma to frown.
For some reason, he sensed no fear from King Hkum, unlike before, when he always shivered under his aura. Now, he seemed more confident, and from his tone, there is even a touch of ruthlessness.
That made him frown.
But then, remembering who was backing him, he smirked and also moved back.

"You already heard what he said. There will be no surrender, so go all out and make sure not even one is left breathing." The moment King Balma gave the order, his thousands of warriors dashed forward, running toward the rebel army.
The Foxkin, Catkin, and Tigerkin warriors of the rebel army shuddered, seeing the sea of beasts coming at them.
To be honest, most of them only dressed up for this war simply because their kings told them they would be receiving reinforcements from a reliable helper.
Now, looking at Kaizo and the legion being referred to as the reinforcement, all these people started considering the idea of running away.
In their heads, live today and die tomorrow.
However, those who had some backbone couldn’t help but wonder why Kaizo and the others seemed happy watching thousands of enemies running at them.
It didn’t take long for them to know why.
Kaizo walked to the front of the line, lightning dancing across his skin.

"Remember, although we got our asses handed to us by those immortals, which I will be frank, had stained our flawless records, our battle spirit still burns bright, so let’s use these lost souls to cleanse our bodies before going out there again."
The legion nodded.
They would most certainly love to commit a slaughter to wipe away the humiliation of their recent defeat.
"Very well then. Let the slaughter begin."
"Hahahahaha!" Lani’s laughter spread as she vanished into a shadow. The next second, she appeared at the center of the enemy’s charge.
Five heads fell the next second.
"Here I come."
Kaizo also descended into battle, obliterating hundreds of enemies at once.
Kaizo had already reached the Spirit King stage, but his battle power, even without his bloodline, was comparable to a Spirit Lord. So these losers had no idea what danger they had walked into.

Veera unleashed only ten undead Angels, who were Spirit Lords. They were the weakest so far in her undead legion. As for Shade King Nykali, he was able to lower his standards to only fifteen Spirit Lord Wraiths.
They couldn’t release more than that, or else they would deprive their teammates of the chance to kill some enemies.
If they go all out, the battle will end within minutes.
In no time, the enemy was stopped from getting even near the rebel army.

Unity, Alina, Velyra, Ingrid, and Val were the only ones standing on the side since they hadn’t fully recovered yet. The rest joined in, with even a few of the Eternal Wraith Legion, who were also hurt, joining the battle.
Vexthra looked at King Hkum and smiled. "You can join the battle now. My people will make sure no harm comes to your people, so kill to your heart’s content. You deserve that much."
Although still in great shock, King Hkum nodded and commanded his men to join. "Kill them all."
They charged and soon were in the mix.
King Balma, who was looking for a quick and decisive massacre, was left staring at the massacre happening before his eyes.
He expected things to go in his favour, but now, he is on the losing side, and he knew there was no turning back now.
When he recovered from his shock, he retrieved an item and crushed it, opening a portal. From within, figures dressed in dark robes walked out.
There were thirty-four of them, each a Heavenly Ascension stage warrior.
One of them turned to King Balma, about to ask him a question, when a pair of identical twins materialized from thin air.
"Oh my, what do we have here?" Olive said, giving a beautiful yet chilling smile to the thirty-four people who immediately broke into a sweat.

chapters.title: Chapter 1166: Long Overdue Battle (2)
paragraphs: Obviously, what could have been a smile that warms the heart had become somewhat nightmarish for the 34 people sent from a Supreme High World to come aid the puppet king Balma.
Olive and her twin sister Ivy are Empyreans, so just their smile, which contains their killing intent, is enough to weaken their resolve.
But even if it wasn’t their smile that was contagious, the fact that these two came from the 14th level of hell said all there is to say.
They are dangerous, and the 34 could see.
They tried to run back into the portal, saving their skin in the process. That was the only logical thing they could do, after all.

But to their shock, a middle-aged man eating grapes stood before the portal with a relaxed expression. None of them realized when he appeared, but there he stood, a smile playing on his lips as he bit into a grape.
Naturally, seeing the smile on Uncle Drew’s face is like staring in the face of death. If Olive and Ivy were a danger, then this man created danger.
"Oh, looks like running is not an option, losers," Ivy said, spinning her dagger between her fingers as she and her sister walked slowly toward the 34 warriors.
King Balma broke into a cold sweat in an instant.
He had been promised reinforcement, and he received it. However, this—this was not something he expected.
His sponsor is someone who has a great interest in this world.
They didn’t say what they wanted, but they planned on making him a king and giving him strength just so they could get access to what they wanted.
They came through on all their promises.
They helped him reach the Heavenly Ascension stage. They helped a few trusted subordinates, too. And now, they had sent the trump cards they promised him.
However, it was all for nothing.
The people he saw as weak turned out to be monsters in sheep’s clothing. They are dangerous, and he can see it now.

Once Ivy and Olive had toyed with their prey enough, they decided to start their torture. The two completely suppressed the 34 warriors, so all that was left was for them to torture and hope they died painfully.
In the distance, too, Kaizo was leading the slaughter.
He was more than willing to fight again, since their last one was nearly a disaster, had Uncle Drew not come to their aid when he did.
Standing far on a mountain, Kent looked at all this and couldn’t help but smile. "Just a year ago, we couldn’t help dreading the day King Balma would attack.
But now, the tables have turned, and he is the one dreading us."
Kent grinned.
He looked at Kaizo and the legion doing what they do best. He also turned to Uncle Drew and, seeing the latter chew on grapes while battle raged on around him, he couldn’t help but smile at all this.
"Looks like he has become much more powerful than he promised he would be the last time we parted. Just what happened to him in his time in the Underworld?"
Kent knew Uncle Drew merely went to the Underworld to get banished souls and used them to create what he called Night Agents.
He had tried it once and it worked, so he went for more. Thankfully, it seems he had succeeded on that front, too. Looking at Olive and Ivy told him all he had to know.
However, he can tell Uncle Drew had become very powerful...too powerful for even him to measure. This got his blood boiling.
He teleported and appeared a meter from Uncle Drew.
"Look who is back," Kent said, smiling at his carriage driver and captain of his Night Riders.
"It is good to be back, young master. I miss you and everyone."
"We miss you, too, Uncle Drew."
King Balma, who saw a familiar face, frowned. He wouldn’t forget Kent since he was the one who poisoned him about three years ago.
Had it not been for Kent, he would have long succeeded in suppressing the rebel alliance and finally becoming the Overlord of Fedora, like he had wanted.
Kent spoiled that plan when he poisoned him, and now, looking at how respectful Uncle Drew is to him, he could tell the reason his warriors were dying in masses was because of him.
This made him sweat even more.
Although nobody was attacking him, he also could not bring himself to attack anyone, thinking that the moment he did, the terrifying man standing before the portal would also attack him.
"Please, order your men to stop. We surrender." Seeing no option left, he knew he could only surrender and hope he would get to save his skin.
However, as if no one had heard him, Uncle Drew and Kent merely focused on their reunion.
"You will have to tell me all there is to know about your journey to the Underworld. However, let’s do that later because right now, we must focus on this portal."
Kent smiled, and Uncle Drew did too.
Since the portal was still open, it meant it was a two-way portal. Since it brought the 34 Heavenly Ascension stage warrior, it could also send them back.
"Let’s see what is on the other side." Uncle Drew nodded, and they walked toward it.
King Balman panicked and was about to speak when a burly man bathed in lightning punched hard in his direction.
"Here I come"
He was forced to defend himself against the punch that could shatter mountains..
But then, when he finished defending against Kaizo’s punch, Kent and Uncle Drew had already entered the portal.
Seeing this, he sighed a little...
"Eyes on me, mister." Kaizo arrived again, and this time, their fists met, creating a thunderclap. They both were pushed back, but a wicked smile appeared on Kaizo’s face.
"This is going to be awesome."
King Balman would dread the day he met the unyielding Kaizo, who seemed to cherish the chaos of battle.
On the other side, Kent and Uncle Drew appeared in a world Kent instantly hated.
It wasn’t because it was a human world, and that he was disgusted by how they were supporting a tyrant to slaughter the innocent.
The hate came from the message he saw, thanks to his Heavenly Jade Eyes.
⟦You have arrived on Planet Hamkin, world of the Earth and Ice Humans⟧
⟦They were ones under the leadership of the benevolent king until he was betrayed by a Tyrant who went into an alliance with the forsaken race⟧
Seeing this message, Kent immediately understood why Fedora was their target. They wanted the planet to become home to the forsaken race, just like how the Hand tried to do with Sonox.
This caused his anger to explode.
However, the next second, thousands of warriors surrounded them, their weapons pointed at Uncle Drew and him.
"Surrender and let yourself be captured. Resist and you die," an Ice Human with blue hair said, his expression filled with anger.
Kent and Uncle Drew said nothing.
Uncle Drew even threw a grape into his mouth and started chewing. He seemed to have picked up a grape addiction since he returned from the Underworld.
Seeing this clear provocation, the Ice Human exploded in anger. However, before he could say anything, Kent asked a rather simple question...
"How long have you been working for the forsaken race?"
Hearing this question, all of them frowned, some even breaking into a sweat. They clearly didn’t expect an outsider to ask this question, not when it was meant to be a secret.
"KILL THEM!"

sentences.text: Obviously, what could have been a smile that warms the heart had become somewhat nightmarish for the 34 people sent from a Supreme High World to come aid the puppet king Balma.
Olive and her twin sister Ivy are Empyreans, so just their smile, which contains their killing intent, is enough to weaken their resolve.
But even if it wasn’t their smile that was contagious, the fact that these two came from the 14th level of hell said all there is to say.
They are dangerous, and the 34 could see.
They tried to run back into the portal, saving their skin in the process.
That was the only logical thing they could do, after all.
But to their shock, a middle-aged man eating grapes stood before the portal with a relaxed expression.
None of them realized when he appeared, but there he stood, a smile playing on his lips as he bit into a grape.
Naturally, seeing the smile on Uncle Drew’s face is like staring in the face of death.
If Olive and Ivy were a danger, then this man created danger.
"Oh, looks like running is not an option, losers," Ivy said, spinning her dagger between her fingers as she and her sister walked slowly toward the 34 warriors.
King Balma broke into a cold sweat in an instant.
He had been promised reinforcement, and he received it.
However, this—this was not something he expected.
His sponsor is someone who has a great interest in this world.
They didn’t say what they wanted, but they planned on making him a king and giving him strength just so they could get access to what they wanted.
They came through on all their promises.
They helped him reach the Heavenly Ascension stage.
They helped a few trusted subordinates, too.
And now, they had sent the trump cards they promised him.
However, it was all for nothing.
The people he saw as weak turned out to be monsters in sheep’s clothing.
They are dangerous, and he can see it now.
Once Ivy and Olive had toyed with their prey enough, they decided to start their torture.
The two completely suppressed the 34 warriors, so all that was left was for them to torture and hope they died painfully.
In the distance, too, Kaizo was leading the slaughter.
He was more than willing to fight again, since their last one was nearly a disaster, had Uncle Drew not come to their aid when he did.
Standing far on a mountain, Kent looked at all this and couldn’t help but smile.
"Just a year ago, we couldn’t help dreading the day King Balma would attack.
But now, the tables have turned, and he is the one dreading us."
Kent grinned.
He looked at Kaizo and the legion doing what they do best.
He also turned to Uncle Drew and, seeing the latter chew on grapes while battle raged on around him, he couldn’t help but smile at all this.
"Looks like he has become much more powerful than he promised he would be the last time we parted.
Just what happened to him in his time in the Underworld?"
Kent knew Uncle Drew merely went to the Underworld to get banished souls and used them to create what he called Night Agents.
He had tried it once and it worked, so he went for more.
Thankfully, it seems he had succeeded on that front, too.
Looking at Olive and Ivy told him all he had to know.
However, he can tell Uncle Drew had become very powerful...too powerful for even him to measure.
This got his blood boiling.
He teleported and appeared a meter from Uncle Drew.
"Look who is back," Kent said, smiling at his carriage driver and captain of his Night Riders.
"It is good to be back, young master.
I miss you and everyone."
"We miss you, too, Uncle Drew."
King Balma, who saw a familiar face, frowned.
He wouldn’t forget Kent since he was the one who poisoned him about three years ago.
Had it not been for Kent, he would have long succeeded in suppressing the rebel alliance and finally becoming the Overlord of Fedora, like he had wanted.
Kent spoiled that plan when he poisoned him, and now, looking at how respectful Uncle Drew is to him, he could tell the reason his warriors were dying in masses was because of him.
This made him sweat even more.
Although nobody was attacking him, he also could not bring himself to attack anyone, thinking that the moment he did, the terrifying man standing before the portal would also attack him.
"Please, order your men to stop.
We surrender." Seeing no option left, he knew he could only surrender and hope he would get to save his skin.
However, as if no one had heard him, Uncle Drew and Kent merely focused on their reunion.
"You will have to tell me all there is to know about your journey to the Underworld.
However, let’s do that later because right now, we must focus on this portal."
Kent smiled, and Uncle Drew did too.
Since the portal was still open, it meant it was a two-way portal.
Since it brought the 34 Heavenly Ascension stage warrior, it could also send them back.
"Let’s see what is on the other side." Uncle Drew nodded, and they walked toward it.
King Balman panicked and was about to speak when a burly man bathed in lightning punched hard in his direction.
"Here I come"
He was forced to defend himself against the punch that could shatter mountains..
But then, when he finished defending against Kaizo’s punch, Kent and Uncle Drew had already entered the portal.
Seeing this, he sighed a little...
"Eyes on me, mister." Kaizo arrived again, and this time, their fists met, creating a thunderclap.
They both were pushed back, but a wicked smile appeared on Kaizo’s face.
"This is going to be awesome."
King Balman would dread the day he met the unyielding Kaizo, who seemed to cherish the chaos of battle.
On the other side, Kent and Uncle Drew appeared in a world Kent instantly hated.
It wasn’t because it was a human world, and that he was disgusted by how they were supporting a tyrant to slaughter the innocent.
The hate came from the message he saw, thanks to his Heavenly Jade Eyes.
⟦You have arrived on Planet Hamkin, world of the Earth and Ice Humans⟧
⟦They were ones under the leadership of the benevolent king until he was betrayed by a Tyrant who went into an alliance with the forsaken race⟧
Seeing this message, Kent immediately understood why Fedora was their target.
They wanted the planet to become home to the forsaken race, just like how the Hand tried to do with Sonox.
This caused his anger to explode.
However, the next second, thousands of warriors surrounded them, their weapons pointed at Uncle Drew and him.
"Surrender and let yourself be captured.
Resist and you die," an Ice Human with blue hair said, his expression filled with anger.
Kent and Uncle Drew said nothing.
Uncle Drew even threw a grape into his mouth and started chewing.
He seemed to have picked up a grape addiction since he returned from the Underworld.
Seeing this clear provocation, the Ice Human exploded in anger.
However, before he could say anything, Kent asked a rather simple question...
"How long have you been working for the forsaken race?"
Hearing this question, all of them frowned, some even breaking into a sweat.
They clearly didn’t expect an outsider to ask this question, not when it was meant to be a secret.
"KILL THEM!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1167: Long Overdue Battle (3)
paragraphs: "KILL THEM"
The order came from a tower standing 70,000 km away.
The moment it did, every last warrior charged forward, aiming for Kent and Uncle Drew’s lives.
Their secret must die with Kent and Uncle Drew, who had casually invaded their planet using a portal meant for their warriors sent to Fedora.
Thousands charged at Uncle Drew and Kent, and thousands more started arriving on the scene.

The last thing they wanted was for their secret to be leaked to the outside. That would be certain death for everyone, including children. They knew the universe hates the forsaken race and those who sympathize with them.
All those affiliated with them are prosecuted and killed without any mercy.
During the Primordial Era, the forsaken race caused so much harm, killing many regardless of their nature or origin. Many innocents died due to their evil ways.
It got to the point that the heavens had to intervene. Thanks to their intervention, the forsaken race was sealed in their worlds and could not leave.
They even made sure that no matter how strong they were, they would remain sealed in their world.
Of course, the rules did apply to all those who would aid them. However, there is a punishment for them.
The heavens would mark them as traitors, and as such, killing them all would be doing the universe a big favor.
All those who kill sympathizers of the forsaken race gain favours from the universe in the form of good karma. So whenever a world is marked as traitors, not even children will be spared.
It is a dark universe after all.
However, there are loopholes to everything. The forsaken race had found them, and through the allies they formed with the normal worlds, they started worming their way back into the universe.
Naturally, Kent was unfriendly toward them.
They took his one true love from him, and for that, he would make them pay. He had already recovered enough of Chaos’s memories and saw how Elina’s death had changed Chaos.
Back then, became so bitter that when he finally came from the Blood System, worlds bled.
He killed so much that it got to the point that all worlds that had dealings with the forsaken race started confessing in an attempt to save their skins.
However, regardless of their pleas, overnight, millions would die.
That was how much Chaos hated the forsaken race, and now, he still seems to hate them.
So, watching thousands of warriors who were affiliated with the forsaken race charge at them, his anger boiled up.
Kent’s bloodline power and blood seals exploded, and at once, all the warriors charging at him came to a halt and dropped to their knees.
Those flying in the air crashed to the ground, raising dust.
"I was prepared to only kill the leader of this planet and his immediate subordinates for bringing chaos into a world under my guardianship.
However, now that I know you people are affiliated with the forsaken race, I am going to kill all warriors regardless of whether you knew or not.
Merely having leaders who went into bed with the forsaken race is a stain on your records, and for that, you all must die."
There was no remorse in Kent’s eyes.
The current him is akin to when Chaos found Elina’s body.
His anger is now controlling his heart. However, despite that, he knew his limit and, like Chaos, he would not kill children, pregnant women, and those who couldn’t even lift a sword.
However, he will kill all warriors, for that is a promise he made to himself many years ago and will keep to the day all forsaken race is eradicated completely.
"Once all warriors are dead, this planet will be sealed and turned into a low world where cultivation will be a thing of the past."
Even Uncle Drew seemed shocked by what Kent had just said. Downgrading a planet from High to Low is not possible.
But then again, this is Kent...
Uncle Drew understood that when it comes to Kent, there is no telling what is possible and what is not. He is a mystery nobody will be able to understand.
Soon, screams started echoing everywhere.
Thousands of doom shards kept bursting out of the ground, drawing holes through hearts, heads, chests, and many more. It was a gory sight, yet necessary.
’No mercy for the evil ones, I suppose. They called this on themselves.’
Uncle Drew just stood on the side, eating his grapes as he watched the massacre Kent was committing.

"Please, show some mercy. We had no choice but to accept their offer. If we had rejected them, then they would one day come back to kill us," the man who gave the order from the tower several miles away appeared 30 km from Kent and tried to reason with him.
Kent raised his cold eyes and stared at him.
"If the forsaken race came, they would have killed everyone, including babies. At least I will be sparing babies and non-warriors."
With that response, the massacre continued, and all the poor souls could do was wait for their turn.
In no time, tens of thousands had died, but Kent was not slowing down at all.
He may be cheerful and kind. However, when he is angry, he will do everything in his power to make sure the source of his anger is eradicated.
He will eradicate the forsaken race and their helpers one day. For now, he will start with those who choose to go against the universe’s mandate and side with the forsaken race.
Meanwhile, back in Fedora, Kaizo and his team were also committing a massacre. They were keeping to their word and making sure they killed all and took no surrenders.
Kaizo had already broken a few bones in King Balma’s body. And he is working toward breaking a few more.
"Please, stop this madness. We want to surrender," King Balma, who was sent crashing into a mountain, said, struggling to stand.
Kaizo hovered in the air, smirked. "If the tables were to turn and you were in our place, would you have accepted our surrender?"
King Balma couldn’t answer. He knew, deep down, that he would laugh and order his men to butcher everyone. He was the kind of savage who takes pleasure in others’ suffering.
He had killed thousands already to reach where he was now. So he most certainly would have cherished the idea of accepting no surrender.

"That is what I thought," Kaizo sneered and broke his knuckles, creating a bone-breaking sound. "Just because you had the strength doesn’t mean you can be arrogant. Trust me, I learned it the hard way.
But then again, when the odds are in your favor, there is no telling what you can do. The point is, you messed with the wrong crowd, and now your reckoning is upon you.
So keep quiet and suffer. Believe me, you will soon have an eternal sleep to think about your life choices."
Kaizo charged at King Balma, who kept taking out one life-saving treasure after another. Eventually, he ran out of life-saving treasures, and so he could only endure the heavy punches landing on him.
Olive and Ivy were also torturing the 34 Heavenly Ascension Stage warriors. They were still alive, but looking at the pain they were in, death would be a mercy to them at this point.
The rest of the legion and Kent’s wives were also having quality time with the orcs and their allies.
All in all, it was a one-sided massacre that would usher the world of Fedora into a new age of peace, one born out of blood.

chapters.title: Chapter 1168: Commanding the Universe
paragraphs: It didn’t take long for the battle on Fedora to come to an end.
As promised by King Hkum before the battle, every last Orc, Hellhoundkin, Lionkin, Rabbitkin, and Batkin was killed. That is how thorough they went.
They knew for a fact that as long as there were more worries, the chances of one of them coming back one day for revenge were high. So it was better to eradicate them all.
Now, the five races that had created chaos in the once peaceful world would be suppressed by the Foxkin, Tigerkin, and Catkins.
All three of them were under Kent’s protection, so the five traitors would be under Kent’s authority.
Rebelling ever again would not cross their feeble minds. It was a win-win situation for both races, and that alone was more than one could ask for.
The Orc King had been beaten to death by the unyielding Kaizo, who cherished every moment of their battle. He had already suffered a crashing defeat against the immortals, so he enjoyed this win.
But by the time everything was said and done, the battle happening on planet Hamkin had also drawn to a close, with 670,000 warriors slaughtered in under an hour.
Kent kept his promise and slaughtered every last warrior.
By the time he was done, the strongest person on Hamkin was not even at the Core Formation stage. That was how thoroughly he ensured the universe’s traitors were eradicated.
"So now that you have killed everyone, what would you gain from this?" the leader of planet Hamkin asked. Kent had spared him for last.
"Who said I did this for any gain?" Kent sneered. "Whatever I did was for personal satisfaction. I made a promise to myself that until every last forsaken soul is eradicated, I will never rest.
You and your people happen to be collateral damage and a necessary massacre to send a message to the forsaken race that their worst nightmare had been reborn.
Be happy, though, since you won’t be the last lost souls I will be sending to the underworld." The man shivered, feeling his soul cry for help, yet he knew no help would come.
Because of their dealings with the forsaken race, they had limited their presence in the universe, always keeping to themselves so that they wouldn’t draw any attention.
Attempting to take control of Fedora was a calculated move.
They planned to use King Balma to rule it, and then, when they were done with their preparation, they would unleash the forsaken race there and let them do the dirty work of killing every last soul.
It was a brilliant plan that wouldn’t be traced back to them.
Unfortunately for them, Kent arrived just when they were drawing near their goal.
"You know, thanking me should be the best thing you can do now. Because of me, your people will keep growing till the world explodes, which it never will.

By killing you scums, the forsaken race cannot come to your world. They will also not have a way to dominate Fedora. So, in a way, they will have to turn elsewhere, and I will be waiting for them there too.
So your death is rather good for peace and prosperity. You should thank me," Kent smiled, and then he commanded a dark shard from the ground to pierce through the man’s head.
He died, and his memories were absorbed by Kent, who immediately sat down to check through and pick the things he wanted.
First, he wanted the location of the forsaken world that had been in contact with this man. Since he was the leader, it was only right that he and they would be in contact.
Kent needed their location or at least a clue. He would certainly be happy to have his hand on the first forsaken world, where killing every soul would feel like soul cleansing for him.
There are no innocents in the forsaken race after all. They are all twisted inside and would do anything to make sure they are the last ones standing.
When they killed Elina, they weren’t after anything in particular. They merely stood up one day and chose to go on a rampage.
All the billions they killed, they had no justification or reason to warrant their deaths. To them, it was merely killing to their heart’s content.
So Kent too wanted the same. He, too, would kill them, but with a motive in mind, and that was his revenge, which he had started since the beginning of time.
After an hour, Kent was done looking through the man’s memories.
’Looks like they too were taking orders from others who are the true people linked to the forsaken race, or at least that is what he thought.’ Kent took a deep breath.
’It doesn’t matter. Chaos had to kill hundreds of worlds before getting his first true intel on the forsaken race’s whereabouts. I will just follow up and make sure they pay for their crimes.’
"How did things go?" Uncle Drew asked. He didn’t even lift a single finger in the massacre that had just ended. It was all Kent who quelled his anger and dispensed justice.
"I got a location, but it is far from this place. The bastard broke the item he used to communicate with them before he died."
"Very loyal of him." Both Uncle Drew and Kent smiled.
"That he was. However, that doesn’t mean he saved them. The least he did was buy them some time."

Uncle Drew nodded, and then he looked around, seeing thousands of dead bodies lying everywhere. He waved his hand, and three hooded figures appeared, each radiating the power of a Death Stage cultivator.
"You already know what to do." The three nodded and formed hand seals. In no time, all the bodies were engulfed in green flames.

Soon, not even their bones remained. Getting burned by hell flames meant they didn’t stand a chance. In their place, thousands of green runes rose into the air and moved toward the three hooded figures.
After absorbing all the runes, they vanished back to where they came from.
Kent stood by until they were done.
"Looks like you came back full of surprises, Uncle Drew."
The Night Rider Captain smiled. "It is all thanks to a fateful encounter I had while in the underworld."
"Whatever that encounter was, I want to hear about it once we leave here," Kent said with a smile. Uncle Drew indeed came back full of surprises.
Uncle Drew merely nodded and then looked at the now clean battlefield.
Kent also nodded to this, and then he looked up. "You already know what to do, Universe. Let’s not delay that any longer."
Immediately, Kent said, the spiritual energy in the air began to grow thin. Uncle Drew felt the change and looked at Kent as if he were some kind of monster.
The process was subtle yet visible from the start. In no time, the process came to an end, leaving only spiritual qi in the air.
In the end, the universe didn’t turn the world into a lowly, spiritless place. Instead, it made it a medium world where reaching the Core Formation stage would be nearly impossible.
To Kent, although he didn’t get what he wanted, this, too, could be accepted.
"Let’s go, Uncle Drew. We are done here."
